text.arabic_uthmani: عَٰلِمُ ٱلْغَيْبِ فَلَا يُظْهِرُ عَلَىٰ غَيْبِهِۦٓ أَحَدًا

words.gloss_range: knower, one who knows, or knowing possessor; locally a nominative active-participle title in construct with the unseen
words.root_gloss_range: knowing, recognizing, teaching, informing, learning, and seeking information; locally settled divine knowledge is selected, not teaching or inquiry

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: the genitive unseen field governed by the opening title

words.prose: {{ar:عَٰلِمُ}} ({{tr:ʿālimu}}) opens as a standing title, not as a new event of discovering. Its construct link to {{ar:ٱلْغَيْبِ}} ({{tr:al-ghaybi}}) makes the unseen the title's governed field, so the following non-disclosure clause follows from divine identity: what knows controls what may be made visible. The wider root can move into teaching, informing, learning, or inquiry, but here the active participle keeps knowledge as already possessed before any transfer is discussed. The exclusivity associated with hidden knowledge in 6:59 is recast here as controlled manifestation, not merely possession. Variant readings that make the title accusative or eventive sharpen the contrast: the base reading presents stable authority, and the same section contrasts human future knowing (72:24), this divine knower-title, and later purposive knowing (72:28). The long opening beat lets the title linger before the clipped turn into negation.

topics.headline: construct title governs the unseen
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the opening as a definite divine title whose internal field is the unseen, not as a loose statement about hidden matters.
topics.reason: QAC and attachment evidence parse the word as a masculine singular nominative active participle and first term of an iḍāfa with the following genitive complement.

topics.headline: knowledge precedes communication

topics.reason: The broader root family includes communication and acquisition branches, but the local active-participle title selects settled possession of knowledge before the disclosure verb appears.

topics.headline: variant readings expose title versus event
topics.reader_payoff: The reader can see how the base grammar leans toward stable title even though accepted variants show possible case and eventive pressure.
topics.reason: The variants are useful as contrast, but the local base surface remains the nominative active-participle construct, so they cannot replace the local parse.

topics.headline: section turns human non-knowledge into divine title
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the prior uncertainty handed off to divine mastery of the unseen, with 72:24 and 72:28 framing the same root in different epistemic roles.
topics.reason: The CRITICAL rows give concrete references: 72:24 and 72:28 contrast human and purposive knowing, while 6:59 supports exclusive hidden knowledge recast here as controlled disclosure.

topics.headline: title launches the access rule

topics.reason: The nominal title precedes the negated verbal clause, and attachment evidence links the title clause to the following verbal rule.

topics.headline: measured opening title

words.prose: {{ar:ٱلْغَيْبِ}} ({{tr:al-ghaybi}}) is definite and genitive, so it completes the title rather than floating as an added theme. The construct compresses knower and hidden field into two joined words, and the recitational liaison lets the title flow into its complement. The root's absence and withdrawal pressure keeps the unseen relational: absent to creatures but present to the divine knower. Inside the ayah, this first hidden domain is later repeated as {{ar:غَيْبِهِۦٓ}} ({{tr:ghaybihī}}), moving from what He knows to what He owns and withholds. The same lexical field can mark the believer's posture in 2:3, but here it becomes divine custody.

topics.headline: definite genitive field
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the unseen as the governed field of the title, not as one unspecified secret.
topics.reason: QAC and attachment evidence identify the word as the genitive second term after the active-participle construct head.

topics.headline: hiddenness faces manifestation

topics.reason: The formal rows are supported by the local iḍāfa parse and by the first beat standing before the negated rule.

topics.headline: belief field becomes custody field
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees a familiar unseen field shift from the believer's posture in 2:3 to God's guarded possession here.
topics.reason: The rows cite 2:3 concretely and the local formula pairs the unseen with the divine knower-title.

topics.headline: first unseen returns as possessed unseen
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the ayah move from the known category of unseen to the possessed domain from which access is withheld.
topics.reason: The same root appears first with the article and later with a suffix, a formal change that supports the knowledge-to-ownership movement.

topics.headline: liaison binds construct phrase

topics.reason: The sound row reinforces the grammatically forced construct attachment.

words.prose: {{ar:فَ}} ({{tr:fa-}}) is the hinge between title and rule. It does not merely add another clause; it lets non-disclosure follow from {{ar:عَٰلِمُ ٱلْغَيْبِ}} ({{tr:ʿālimu al-ghaybi}}). Because it is fused on the surface with {{ar:لَا}} ({{tr:lā}}) while remaining a distinct segment, the reader meets consequence and negation in one turn. Across the boundary, the same hinge answers the unresolved timing of 72:25 by moving from human uncertainty to divine access control.

topics.headline: title becomes consequence
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the negated disclosure clause is a consequence of the knower-title, not a detached second statement.
topics.reason: The particle is segmented before the negator and attachment evidence links the title clause to the following verbal clause.

topics.headline: sequence and inference both remain live
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees continuity and inference together: the title is resumed, and a rule is drawn from it.
topics.reason: The rows' double function fits the local position between a nominal title beat and a negated verbal clause.

topics.headline: surface fusion keeps two mechanisms

topics.reason: The surface joins the connector to the negator, while QAC segmentation still treats the connector as its own word.

topics.reason: The boundary rows explicitly connect the particle to the unresolved timing in 72:25 and the access rule in 72:26.

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: the indicative imperfect disclosure verb governed by the negator

words.prose: {{ar:لَا}} ({{tr:lā}}) opens a standing denial, not a command to an addressee. It governs {{ar:يُظْهِرُ}} ({{tr:yuẓhiru}}) as an indicative imperfect, while its surface fusion with the preceding connector makes inference and denial arrive together. Its scope then stretches through the domain phrase to final {{ar:أَحَدًا}} ({{tr:aḥadan}}), where the negative-polarity object makes the restriction exhaustive: not a single possible recipient is disclosed upon His unseen. The result is not one refused disclosure event but a rule, while 72:27 can still introduce a selected exception.

topics.headline: standing fact, not prohibition
topics.reader_payoff: The reader recognizes a stated divine practice rather than an instruction telling someone not to seek access.
topics.reason: QAC parses the negated verb as indicative imperfect, and attachment evidence treats the particle as scoping over the verbal complement.

topics.headline: negation reaches the final indefinite
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees how the denial starts at the verb and becomes exhaustive when it lands on the final indefinite object.
topics.reason: The polarity profile marks the final object form as negative-polarity friendly, and local syntax places it under the negator's scope.

topics.headline: inference and denial arrive together
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the causal hinge and the negator fused on the surface while the negator still governs the verb.
topics.reason: The written surface compresses connector and negator, but QAC segmentation keeps the negative particle analytically distinct.

topics.headline: whole access event under denial
topics.reader_payoff: The reader meets blocked disclosure before any recipient is named, so the recipient arrives inside an already closed access frame.
topics.reason: The clause order places negation and verb first, then the domain phrase, and only then the final object.

words.gloss_range: makes manifest, discloses, grants access, or causes to appear; locally a negated Form IV imperfect with explicit recipient and domain complement
words.root_gloss_range: appearing, being exterior, making visible, exposing, backing, supporting, and prevailing; locally causative disclosure over the unseen is denied

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: the negator governing the disclosure verb
the prepositional domain phrase governed by the disclosure verb
the explicit recipient object delayed to the clause ending

words.prose: {{ar:يُظْهِرُ}} ({{tr:yuẓhiru}}) names the denied act as causative disclosure. The verb is indicative under {{ar:لَا}} ({{tr:lā}}), so it states an ongoing rule rather than a command. Its argument frame separates roles: the divine subject is implicit from the title, {{ar:عَلَىٰ غَيْبِهِۦٓ}} ({{tr:ʿalā ghaybihī}}) marks the domain, and {{ar:أَحَدًا}} ({{tr:aḥadan}}) is the recipient. The visibility root gives disclosure the force of making hidden reality appear, with exterior-surface and over-domain pressure making it more than informing: it would be exposure and vantage over the hidden field. The Form IV stem keeps that access as something God would cause, not something a recipient achieves. The Form I variant contrast narrows the point: the base wording denies granted access, while 72:27 later states the authorized exception. The same controlled-action pressure contrasts with routed punishment in 72:17 and public prevalence in 9:33; here the action withheld is access to the unseen. The verb also sits inside a hidden-visible-hidden frame, and its forceful emergence sound collides with the surrounding concealment.

topics.headline: indicative imperfect states regulated disclosure
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees ongoing divine regulation of disclosure, not a one-time refusal or a command to humans.
topics.reason: QAC identifies an active 3ms indicative imperfect under non-jussive negation.

topics.headline: subject, domain, and recipient are separated
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that God controls the act, the unseen is the domain, and the final object is only the possible recipient.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence gives an implicit 3ms subject from the title, an explicit object at the final word, and a prepositional complement for the possessed unseen.

topics.headline: manifestation exposes the hidden field
topics.reader_payoff: The reader feels disclosure as exposure of what is hidden, including the denied vantage over the domain.
topics.reason: The root's visibility and over-domain senses are locally licensed by the Form IV verb plus the following preposition.

topics.headline: Form IV makes access caused, not self-acquired
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees that access would have to be caused by the divine discloser; recipients do not break into the unseen.
topics.reason: The local form is Form IV active, and the object/preposition frame supports causative disclosure.

topics.headline: Form I contrast cannot replace local transitivity
topics.reader_payoff: The reader can see why the base Form IV wording matters: it denies granted access to a recipient, not mere appearance.
topics.reason: The Form I variant is useful contrast, but the base form and explicit object keep the local reading transitive and causative.

topics.headline: controlled divine action contrasts across scenes
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the same controlled-action pressure applied differently: punishment is routed in 72:17, public prevalence is granted in 9:33, but unseen access is withheld here.
topics.reason: The rows give concrete references and are kept as contrasts, not as alternate local senses.

topics.headline: visibility verb interrupts repeated hiddenness
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the disclosure verb sitting between two hiddenness terms, so manifestation is framed as a controlled breach of the hidden field.
topics.reason: The rare pairing of the visibility root with the hiddenness root is locally visible in the ayah's word order.

topics.headline: verb opens frame before domain and recipient
topics.reader_payoff: The reader meets disclosure as the frame first, then the guarded field, and only at the end the excluded recipient.
topics.reason: The local sequence is negated verb, prepositional domain, then final object.

topics.headline: denied verb prepares the exception
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees 72:27 as specifying the denied disclosure verb rather than starting a separate subject.
topics.reason: The boundary rows connect commanded human non-knowledge to divine disclosure control and to the exception in 72:27.

topics.headline: forceful emergence sound
topics.reader_payoff: The reader can hear the disclosure verb as a forceful emergence sound inside a field of concealment.
topics.reason: The sound rows reinforce the contrast between manifesting and hiddenness already established by the lexical frame.

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: the possessed unseen governed by the preposition

words.prose: {{ar:عَلَىٰ}} ({{tr:ʿalā}}) prevents the verb from becoming simple information transfer to a recipient. It governs {{ar:غَيْبِهِۦٓ}} ({{tr:ghaybihī}}), placing the denied disclosure over a protected domain before {{ar:أَحَدًا}} ({{tr:aḥadan}}) arrives. Its over/upon pressure makes access feel like privileged vantage over the unseen, while the syntax keeps the final word as the affected recipient rather than the governed field. The long domain phrase gives the guarded unseen audible weight and carries the unresolved term from 72:25 into the field over which no general disclosure is granted.

topics.headline: preposition marks domain, not mere recipient direction
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees disclosure as access over His unseen, not simply information sent to someone.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence marks the following possessed unseen as the prepositional complement governed by this preposition.

topics.headline: over-position gives privileged vantage
topics.reader_payoff: The reader feels the denied access as privileged vantage over a domain, not flat receipt of data.
topics.reason: The semantic pressure of over/upon is locally constrained by the governed domain phrase.

topics.headline: prepositional layer splits domain from object
topics.reader_payoff: The reader meets the protected field before the excluded recipient, so the clause remains domain-centered.
topics.reason: The local frame contains a prepositional complement before the explicit direct object.

topics.headline: domain phrase carries boundary pressure
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears and sees the unknown term from 72:25 moved into the guarded domain before any recipient is named.
topics.reason: The boundary row gives the concrete prior reference, and the sound row reinforces the length of the domain phrase.

words.gloss_range: His unseen, His hidden domain, or the possessed unseen; locally a genitive prepositional complement with a 3ms suffix referring back to the divine title
words.root_gloss_range: absence, hiddenness, withdrawal, and hidden locus or time; locally the same unseen field is made possessed and governed

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: the final excluded recipient after the possessed domain

words.prose: {{ar:غَيْبِهِۦٓ}} ({{tr:ghaybihī}}) repeats the hiddenness root but adds the suffix, so the unseen is no longer only the known field of the title; it is His owned domain. That suffix makes disclosure a matter of permission from the possessor, not successful investigation by outsiders, and it compresses owner and noun into one word instead of repeating a divine name. The hidden-locus pressure makes the possessed unseen feel like a governed field or setting, while the recitational length lets that owned domain linger. Positioned before {{ar:أَحَدًا}} ({{tr:aḥadan}}), the possessed domain is secured before any recipient is named. The boundary also shifts from the speaker's relation to God in 72:25 to God's own possession of the unseen. This closure prepares 72:27: any exception is a grant from the owner of the unseen, not a loophole in the denial.

topics.headline: suffix makes unseen a divine possession
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the unseen as owned by the divine referent, not as anonymous hidden territory.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence routes the 3ms suffix back to the divine title and parses the noun as governed by the preceding preposition.

topics.headline: hiddenness becomes jurisdiction

topics.reason: The root's hidden-domain pressure is locally sharpened by the suffix and by the prepositional domain frame.

topics.headline: hidden place-field image is supporting pressure

topics.headline: affixal economy keeps ownership central
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees ownership compressed into the noun itself and hears the possessed domain linger before the final exclusion.

topics.headline: possessive orientation shifts to His unseen
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the boundary preserve the divine referent while shifting from the speaker's relation to God in 72:25 to God's own possession of the unseen in 72:26.

topics.headline: preposition and domain flow together

words.prose: {{ar:أَحَدًا}} ({{tr:aḥadan}}) arrives last as the direct object, so the recipient role is delayed until the verb and guarded domain have already dominated the clause. Because the word is indefinite and singular under {{ar:لَا}} ({{tr:lā}}), it means not even one possible recipient; the singular noun-number form distributes the denial one by one rather than narrowing it or grouping recipients as a mass. Its bare tanwīn form is not limited to an addressed group, and its accusative role keeps the possible recipient passive: no one makes themselves privy to the unseen. The same-surah singular guardrail reaches this access question after earlier association warnings such as 72:18, while 18:26 supplies a narrowed parallel for exclusive prerogative in judgment rather than unseen access. The final -an cadence separates the excluded recipient from the repeated hidden domain, and the final landing prepares 72:27, where the universal baseline is narrowed only by selected permission.

topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees that the singular under negation expands to no one at all, not to one particular denied person.
topics.reason: The contextual polarity profile marks this form as negative-polarity friendly, and the local word is indefinite under the negator.

topics.headline: bare tanwīn form avoids group limits

topics.reason: The word is bare, singular, accusative, and indefinite, with no suffix limiting it to a local addressee group.

topics.reason: The rows cite same-surah occurrences at 72:2, 72:7, 72:18, 72:20, and 72:22, with 72:18 giving the clearest guardrail parallel.

topics.reason: The parallel is concrete and useful, but it must be narrowed to a shared exclusion pattern because the governed domain differs.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: The construct 'knower of the unseen,' the repeated ghayb/ghaybihi, causative yuzhiru, and indefinite ahadan under negation.
baseline_models.mechanism: Clear apprehension remains with the knower while a causative transition from concealment into visibility or access is withheld from the entire recipient class.

activation_trace.role: The image of a thing becoming clear to its knower makes the opening noun the source-side possession of clarity.
The image of being hidden from sight or knowledge defines the domain whose two mentions bind object and possession.
Coming out into view supplies the outward transition that the causative verb places under divine control.
Exhaustive 'anyone' under negation closes the ordinary recipient class without leaving a numerical loophole.

changed_reading.before: God knows the unseen and does not tell anyone.
changed_reading.after: The ayah presents a controlled boundary: divine clarity does not automatically become creaturely visibility or access.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: The repeated ghayb, causative yuzhiru, and the preposition ala permit a depth-to-surface reading internal to the focus wording.
baseline_models.mechanism: The hidden is pictured as depth or buried structure, while disclosure is emergence onto an outer surface or acquisition of access over it; no one is independently raised into that vantage.

activation_trace.role: A low place in which something disappears gives the unseen a concealed depth rather than only an abstract unknownness.
Hidden roots beneath earth supply a structured interior whose effects may exist without the structure being exposed.
The upper or outer surface provides the opposite layer toward which disclosure would move concealed depth.
Finding out or gaining access turns surface emergence into an epistemic vantage over the hidden domain.

changed_reading.before: The verse contrasts known and unknown information.
changed_reading.after: It also maps a protected topology: concealed depth is not opened into a surface on which an observer may stand.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: The possessive 'His unseen' combines with ala, yuzhiru, and ahadan.
baseline_models.mechanism: The verb can carry elevation or overcoming as well as visibility, so the negation denies installation of any creature in a position of mastery over the possessed hidden domain.

activation_trace.role: Clear apprehension locates epistemic competence at the divine source.
Concealment supplies the domain explicitly retained as 'His.'
Being over or overcoming makes disclosure potentially a grant of rank and control, which the negation refuses.
Exhaustive negation denies that jurisdiction to every possible creaturely claimant.

changed_reading.before: Disclosure would merely add information to a recipient.
changed_reading.after: Unrestricted disclosure would install a rival epistemic master, and the ayah denies that transfer of standing.

context_deltas.mechanism: The opening sequence supplies a communication pipeline from concealed casting, through speech becoming outward, to acoustic reception; the focus ayah governs who may initiate that conversion from hidden knowledge into a hearable signal.

activation_trace.role: Hiddenness supplies the latent source state of the communication chain.
Coming into view supplies the controlled transition from latent content to an outwardly available form.
Casting knowledge secretly supplies a nonpublic transfer at the first stage of the relay.
Speech held within and not yet manifested supplies the latent verbal pole from which utterance can emerge.
Producing speech by articulation supplies the outward verbal pole of the same relay.
Auditory perception supplies the receiver endpoint at which disclosed content becomes creaturely evidence.

structural_cues: 72:1 orders command, revelation, listening, reported speech, and a second report of hearing.
The focus ayah places causative manifestation between possessed hiddenness and a potential recipient.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies secret casting, latent and articulated speech, and hearing; I infer a directed hidden-to-audible relay governed by the focus prohibition; alternatively these may be adjacent speech events rather than stages of one channel.

changed_reading.after: The ayah regulates conversion of concealed divine knowledge into utterance that another being can hear.

context_deltas.mechanism: Probing and listening encounter occupied guard positions and surveillance, turning the focus prohibition into an actively enforced perimeter around access to concealed information.

activation_trace.role: A hidden low place gives the protected material an interior location behind the perimeter.
Gaining access names the boundary-crossing action that the focus clause denies.
Seeking or feeling for something supplies active reconnaissance against the boundary.
Literal preservation and guarding supplies the defensive function of the occupied perimeter.
Auditory perception identifies the information-extraction operation attempted at the listening stations.
Sitting in wait for surveillance turns the stations into persistent access posts rather than incidental hearing.
Watchful guarding supplies interception at the attempted breach point.

structural_cues: 72:8-9 moves from touching the sky to finding it filled with guards, then from former listening seats to present interception.
The focus preposition ala supports a contested vantage over the hidden domain.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies reconnaissance, listening posts, guards, and watchers; I infer a security perimeter enforcing the focus rule; alternatively the defended sky may be a concrete episode without exhausting the general disclosure clause.

changed_reading.before: Non-disclosure is a passive absence of information.
changed_reading.after: Non-disclosure is active access control that detects, occupies, and intercepts unauthorized extraction.

context_deltas.mechanism: The following exception does not erase the boundary: selection authorizes a messenger, insertion gives him a path, front and rear delimit it, and watchers escort it, producing a narrow guarded corridor through the prohibition.

activation_trace.role: Exhaustive anyone establishes the default closure against which the following exception has force.
Gaining access supplies what is exceptionally granted in bounded form.
Acceptance rather than displeasure supplies the authorization decision that selects the exception.
Messenger and message supply a role-defined carrier rather than an unrestricted knower.
Inserting one thing into another supplies the controlled placement of protection around the carrier's route.
The interval between two sides supplies the corridor's bounded middle.
The idiom of what lies before the hands supplies the guarded forward side of transmission.
What lies behind supplies the guarded rear side, closing the route in both directions.
Watchful guarding supplies continuous escort and containment along the authorized path.

structural_cues: Illa immediately reverses the default closure for one selected class.
The paired 'before him' and 'behind him' spatially encloses the messenger.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies selection, a messenger, insertion, two-sided enclosure, and watching; I infer a narrow authorized transport corridor rather than wholesale opening of the unseen; alternatively the watchers may protect only the messenger, not delimit information scope.

changed_reading.after: The default is universal closure, but a selected messenger may traverse a tightly bounded and guarded disclosure corridor.

context_deltas.mechanism: The speaker disclaims possession, is limited to delivery, bears messages as a messenger, and is selected rather than self-authorized; disclosure therefore delegates performance without transferring title to the unseen.

activation_trace.role: The possessive hidden domain remains attached to its source even when some content is carried outward.
Being over or dominant frames unrestricted disclosure as a standing that is not ceded.
Ownership and power of disposal supply the expressly disclaimed form of independent agency.
Delivering a message supplies a bounded duty of conveyance rather than proprietary control of its source.
Messenger and message define the agent by commission and carried content.
Acceptance supplies source-side choice rather than recipient-side seizure of authority.

reader_a.activated_readings_md:
1. **Hidden knowledge is selectively disclosed, not generally penetrable.** `عالم` activates ع ل م B001, knowing as something becomes clear; doubled `الغيب/غيبه` activates غ ي ب B001, what is hidden from sight or knowledge; `يظهر` activates ظ ه ر B001 and B008, bringing into view and granting access; `أحدا` activates ء ح د B002. The possessive repetition makes the hidden domain God’s, and the negation blocks exhaustive access. The inferred mechanism is controlled disclosure: becoming visible depends on an act from the knower, not an intruder’s reach. The ayah reads as governance of access rather than mere possession of secret facts.

2. **No one gains the upper hand over the hidden domain.** ظ ه ر B007 means overcoming or being over, activated by the construction `على غيبه`. This branch coexists with disclosure because the next ayah introduces a narrow exception for an accepted messenger surrounded by guards. The inferred relation is that unauthorized “appearance upon” hidden knowledge would amount to mastery over it. The verse denies both uncontrolled revelation and epistemic ascendancy.
reader_a.retrospective_surprises_md: The exception in 72:27 corrects an overbroad reading of `فلا يظهر`: disclosure is possible to an accepted messenger, but the surrounding `رصدا` confirms that it remains selective and governed.

reader_a.activated_readings_md:
1. **The knowledge asymmetry is stated immediately after confessed uncertainty.** Fixed `ع ل م` B001 is knowledge with clarity and distinction, while fixed `غ ي ب` B001 is what is hidden from human sight or knowledge. The nominal `عَٰلِمُ` follows `إِنْ أَدْرِىٓ` in 72:25 without an intervening change of topic. The packet supplies the adjacent contrast; I infer that the messenger's uncertainty is not a defect in the message but a role boundary produced by unequal access. The fixed phrase relocates complete knowledge from the carrier to the possessor of the unseen.

2. **The repeated possessive makes the unseen a controlled domain.** Fixed `غ ي ب` B001 appears first as the category `ٱلْغَيْبِ` and then as `غَيْبِهِۦ`, marked as his. In 72:8-9, a formerly probed upper domain becomes guarded, while 72:27 will place prepared watchers around an approved messenger. The packet supplies hiddenness, possession, and controlled approaches; I infer that the unseen is not merely material nobody happens to know, but information whose access is governed. The second occurrence changes the first from an abstract unknown into a held domain.

3. **`يُظْهِرُ عَلَىٰ` can mean granting access, not merely making visible.** Fixed `ظ ه ر` B001 is bringing something into view, but B008 is finding out or gaining access to hidden information, and the construction retains `عَلَىٰ`. Because the object is precisely `غَيْبِهِۦ` and the next ayah supplies an approved exception, the packet supports both exposure and authorized access. I infer that the governing act is to place someone in a position to know what was hidden. The clause therefore concerns permissioned disclosure, not a contradiction in which the unseen ceases absolutely to be unseen.

4. **The negated singular exhausts unapproved recipients.** Fixed `ء ح د` B002 gives exhaustive "anyone" under negation and B005 can distribute the exclusion person by person. The next word in packet order is the exception `إِلَّا مَنِ ٱرْتَضَىٰ` (72:27). The packet supplies a universal negative followed by a selection condition; I infer that `أَحَدًا` closes every default access slot while leaving only the expressly opened one. The reading changes `فَلَا يُظْهِرُ` from an absolute ban on disclosure into a default-denial policy.

5. **Knowing and showing remain separate operations.** Fixed `ع ل م` B001 describes the subject's complete cognition, whereas `ظ ه ر` B001/B008 describes what another is allowed to see or access. The packet supplies two different predicates with the same unseen object; I infer that possession of knowledge does not mechanically entail publication. The ayah reads as an information boundary: total knowledge at the source, selective visibility downstream.
reader_a.retrospective_surprises_md: Later 72:27 immediately prevents the fixed negation from being misread as absolute nondisclosure: `إِلَّا` opens one approval-based route, and 72:28 audits what that route delivers. The surprise is structural rather than contradictory. Fixed `ء ح د` B002 excludes every default recipient, while `ظ ه ر` B008 access remains possible only through selected, guarded carriage.

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak ifadesi, içine düşülen alçak araziyi, bir şeyi saklayan yeri, kuyu dibini, vadi çukurunu ve çukur araziyi aynı mekansal çekirdekte birleştirir.
identity_judgment.boundary_note: Dal genel görünmezliği değil, bir şeyi gözden saklayabilen alçak veya dip konumlu yeri anlatır; kuyu dibi bunun yapıya bağlı özel gerçekleşmesidir.

lexicalization_scope.note: Tanım, yalın biçimlerdeki çukur yer anlamını özel yapılardaki kuyu veya vadi dibi anlamından ayırır ve yapı içindeki kullanımı genel bir kök anlamına yaymaz.

concept_map.definition: Bir şeyin içine girince gözden saklanabileceği alçak, çukur veya dip konumlu yerdir. Kuyu dibi ve vadi çukuru bu yer türünün belirli yapılara bağlı örnekleridir.

facets.statement: Yer çevresine göre alçak veya çukurdur ve içine giren şeyi gözden saklar.
Belirli bir yapıda kuyunun dibi, saklayıcı çukur yerin özel bir gerçekleşmesidir.
Vadinin çukur kesimi ve çevresine göre basık arazi de aynı mekansal özellik üzerinden adlandırılır.

source_synthesis.common_summary: Kaynaklar, alçaklık ile saklayıcılığı birlikte taşır; genel çukur araziyi, bir şeyin içinde gizlendiği yeri ve kuyu ya da vadi dibini aynı mekansal çerçevede açıklar.

concept_gloss.applicability: Alçaklık veya dipte bulunma ile gözden saklama özelliklerini birlikte taşıyan dalın tamamını karşılar.

error_profile.preserves: Yer biçimini ve bu biçimin içindeki şeyi gözden saklaması sonucunu birlikte korur.

contextual_glosses.applicability: Yalnızca kuyu yapısının en alçak ve saklı kesiminin anlatıldığı özel bağlamda uygundur.

error_profile.preserves: Dipte bulunma ve gözden saklanma özelliklerini korur.
error_profile.loses: Kuyu dışındaki vadi çukurlarını ve genel alçak arazi kullanımını kapsamaz.

contextual_glosses.applicability: Çevresine göre alçakta kalan doğal yer biçimi anlatılırken kullanılır.

error_profile.preserves: Çevresine göre alçak olan yer özelliğini korur.
error_profile.loses: Kuyu dibine bağlı özel kullanımı ve saklayıcılık vurgusunun bir bölümünü dışarıda bırakır.

lexical_glosses.target_gloss: içine gireni gizleyen çukur veya dip yer

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak ifadesi dalı açıkça koruluk ve sık ağaçlık olarak tanımlar, ayrıca adlandırmayı içine girenin gözden kaybolabilmesine bağlar.
identity_judgment.boundary_note: Buradaki referans belirli bir yer adı veya her türlü ağaç topluluğu değil, içine gireni örtebilen sık koruluk türüdür.

lexicalization_scope.note: Tanım yalın dalın sık ağaçlık ve saklayıcı koruluk anlamını verir; yalnız belirli bir yer adına veya başka yapılara ait anlam eklemez.

concept_map.definition: İçine giren kişi veya şeyi gözden saklayabilecek yoğunluktaki ağaçlık ya da koruluktur. Adlandırmanın ayırıcı gerekçesi, ağaçların arasında bulunanın görünmez hale gelmesidir.

facets.statement: Referans, ağaçların toplu ve yoğun bulunduğu bir koruluk veya sık ağaçlıktır.
Ağaçlığın yoğunluğu, içine giren kişi veya şeyin dışarıdan görülmesini engeller.

source_synthesis.common_summary: Kaynaklar, sık ağaçlık veya koruluk referansında birleşir ve adın gerekçesini, içeri girenin bu yoğun bitki örtüsü içinde gözden saklanmasına bağlar.

concept_gloss.applicability: Hem yoğun ağaç topluluğunu hem de bu yoğunluğun saklayıcı etkisini taşıdığı için dalın tam çekirdeğine uygulanır.

error_profile.preserves: Yoğun ağaç topluluğu referansını açık biçimde korur.
error_profile.loses: İçine gireni gözden saklama sonucunu sözün kendisinde açıkça belirtmez.

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak ifadesinin baskın çizgisi, kişiyi yokluğunda kusuruyla anma ve işitirse üzüleceği biçimde onun hakkında konuşmadır; ancak aynı ifade, daha geniş bir aktarımda kişiyi iyi veya kötü anmayı da bildirir.
identity_judgment.boundary_note: Dal yalnız kötülemeye indirgenemez: olumsuz kullanım merkezde olsa da kaynakta kişinin yokluğunda olumlu ya da olumsuz anılması biçiminde daha geniş bir değişke vardır.

lexicalization_scope.note: Tanım, yalın ve türemiş biçimlerdeki yokluğunda anma eylemini, belirli yapının yalnız hazır bulunmama koşulu bildiren işlevinden ayırır.

concept_map.definition: Bir kişiyi hazır bulunmadığı sırada anmak veya onun hakkında konuşmaktır. Kullanımın merkezinde o kişinin kusurunu söylemek, onu kötülemek ya da duysa üzüleceği sözler etmek bulunur; bir kaynak değişkesi ise iyi veya kötü her türlü anmayı kapsar.

facets.statement: Hakkında konuşulan kişi konuşma sırasında hazır bulunmaz.
Baskın kullanımda konuşan kişi, bulunmayan kişinin kusurunu söyler, onu kötüler veya incitecek söz eder.
Daha geniş bir kaynak değişkesinde, bulunmayan kişiyi iyi ya da kötü biçimde anmak yeterlidir.
Belirli bir yapı, sözün hakkında konuşulan kişinin yokluğunda ve arkasından söylendiğini belirtir.

source_synthesis.common_summary: Ortak ağırlık, bulunmayan kişinin kusurunu söyleme, onu kötüleme ve işitirse üzüleceği sözler etme üzerindedir; toplu ifade ayrıca iyi veya kötü anmayı kapsayan daha geniş bir değişkeyi korur.

concept_gloss.text: kişiyi yokluğunda iyi ya da kötü anma

concept_map.definition: Kocası yanında bulunmayan kadının durumunu anlatır. Buna bağlı özel kullanım, kadınların kocalarının yokluğunda onların hoş karşılamayacağı davranışlardan kaçınıp korunması gerekeni gözetmeleridir.

facets.statement: Kadının kocası geçici olarak yanında bulunmaz veya ondan uzaktadır.
Bu yokluk, kocası yanında olmayan kadına özgü bir durum adıyla ifade edilir.
Özel bir yapıda kadın, kocasının yokluğunda onun hoşlanmayacağı davranışlardan kaçınarak bağlılığı ve korunması gerekeni gözetir.

source_synthesis.common_summary: Kaynaklar, kocası yanında bulunmayan kadının durumunda birleşir; ortak toplu ifade ayrıca bu yokluk sırasında kocanın hoş karşılamayacağı davranışlardan sakınmayı bağlı bir kullanım olarak verir.

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak sözü, kocanın eşini evlenmesi sürekli yasak bir kadının sırtına benzeterek kendisine yasak saydığını bildiren belirli sözü ve bunun doğurduğu yükümlülüğü anlatır. Dal çerçevesi bu geleneksel hukuk kullanımını doğru sınırlar.
identity_judgment.boundary_note: Bu dal belirli evlilik sözüne bağlıdır; sırttan, yardımdan veya genel yasaklamadan ibaret değildir.

lexicalization_scope.note: Geleneksel işlem adı ile onu kuran belirli söz kalıbı birlikte, fakat kapsamları belirtilerek tanımlanır.

concept_map.definition: Kocanın eşini, evlenmesi sürekli yasak olan bir kadının sırtına benzeten belirli bir sözle kendisine yasak saydığını bildirmesidir; kaynak bu sözün bir giderim yükümlülüğü doğurduğunu da belirtir.

Bu geleneksel söz, ilişkiye dair bir giderim yükümlülüğü doğurur.

error_profile.preserves: Eşe yöneltilen benzetmeyi, yasaklama bildirimini ve doğan yükümlülüğü korur.

lexicalization_scope.note: Yalın sözlüksel biçimin özel tüy anlamı tanımlanır; genel dış yüz anlamına genişletilmez.

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak sözü bir şeyi sırtın arkasına atma görüntüsünden hareketle unutmayı, önemsememeyi ve ilgilenmeden geride bırakmayı anlatır. Dal çerçevesi bu ihmal çekirdeğini doğru korur.
identity_judgment.boundary_note: Bu dal geriye atıp ihmal etmeyi anlatır; ihtiyaç için yedek tutma ve önlem alma bunun karşıtı yöndedir.

lexicalization_scope.note: İhmal edilen şeyin adı ile bir isteği geriye atma kalıbı ayrı biçimler olarak, aynı ihmal çekirdeğinde tutulur.

concept_gloss.applicability: Bir şeyin unutulduğu, bir isteğin dikkate alınmadığı veya işin ilgisizce geride bırakıldığı bağlamlarda kullanılır.

error_profile.preserves: Geride bırakma işlemini, ilgisizliği ve unutma sonucunu birlikte korur.

branches.neighbor_coverage_note: Adaylar değerlendirildi; hazır tutma dalı, geriye atıp unutma çekirdeğinin en açık karşıt yönünü gösterir.

lexicalization_scope.note: Anlam yalnızca ayıp veya kusurun kişiden uzaklığını bildiren kalıba bağlı tutulur.

concept_map.definition: Bir ayıp, kusur veya suçlamanın kişiye yapışmaması, ondan uzak kalması ve onu sorumlu duruma düşürmemesidir.

facets.statement: Olumsuz nitelik kişiye bağlanmaz ve onun üzerinde kalıcı bir yük oluşturmaz.

source_synthesis.common_summary: Kaynaklar ayıp veya kusurun kişiden uzak kalması ve ona yapışmaması anlamında birleşir.

concept_gloss.applicability: Bir suçlama veya kusurun muhataba bağlanmadığını bildiren kalıplaşmış sözlerde kullanılır.

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak sözü evde bulunan eşya ve giysileri adlandırır, bunların kişiye dayanak ve yedek sağladığı düşüncesini de açıklar. Verilen çerçeve somut eşya çekirdeğini ve bağlı işlevi doğru korur.

lexicalization_scope.note: Yalın sözlüksel biçimin ev eşyası anlamı tanımlanır; dayanak olma yalnızca bu eşyanın işlevsel açıklamasıdır.

source_synthesis.common_summary: Kaynaklar ev eşyası ve giysilerde birleşir; bunların kişiye dayanak sağlamasını adın bağlı açıklaması olarak verir.

concept_gloss.applicability: Evde bulunan eşya ve giysiler, özellikle gerektiğinde yararlanılan birikim olarak düşünüldüğünde kullanılır.

error_profile.preserves: Somut ev eşyasını ve onun dayanak ya da yedek olma işlevini korur.
